query: a configuration change to the address management pipeline caused customer address ranges to stop being announced upstream, leaving their services unreachable until the change was rolled back
build jobs were accepted by the platform but never picked up by any worker, so they sat waiting indefinitely without starting
an edit to the core network configuration took the whole service off the public internet for all customers at once
reordering the clauses of an address advertisement policy stopped a critical set of address blocks from being announced, taking nineteen of the busiest locations offline while the rest kept serving
name lookups stopped resolving for several hours, so clients could not find the addresses of the services they needed

an internal testing component was switched off to work around an incompatibility, and that second change propagated instantly to every server, triggering a scripting error that returned server errors to a quarter of traffic
a social platform disappeared entirely for hours, taking down its own internal tooling at the same time so engineers could not reach the systems they needed to fix it
a simplification of the caching layer configuration introduced a defect that broke package downloads for developers

a misleading comment led an engineer to push a packet filtering rule that silently blocked the return traffic between the load balancers and the web servers, taking every site down until the commit was reverted
a migration left a small fraction of managed databases pointing at a shared storage location instead of their own, so restoring them pulled someone else's data and discarded their recent writes
